why: The Simon of 1:29-30 is Simon Peter, whose mother-in-law Jesus heals; Bible Atlas's second Simon here is Judas Iscariot's father, and Peter's wife is implied but not mentioned. The healing of the paralyzed man comes in 2:1-12, not this chapter. Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but John baptizes in the Jordan near the Judean wilderness (1:4-5, 1:9), much farther south, so no dot is drawn.
1:2 names Isaiah the prophet as the source of the words quoted in 1:2-3; Bible Atlas does not link him in this chapter.
In 2:13 Jesus teaches "along the shore of the sea", the Sea of Galilee beside Capernaum; Bible Atlas does not link it here.
Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but "from across the Jordan" in 3:8 means the land east of the river's middle and lower course (Perea), so no dot is drawn.
In 3:7 Jesus withdraws "to the sea", the Sea of Galilee, where the crowds find him (3:9); Bible Atlas does not link it here.

Mark never uses Jesus' name in chapter 4 (it says only "he"), but he is the one teaching from the boat and calming the storm. "The sea" where he teaches (4:1) and which he calms (4:39) is the Sea of Galilee.
5:1 and 5:21 have Jesus crossing "the sea", the Sea of Galilee, and the pigs rush into it (5:13). The "land of the Gerasenes" (5:1) has no entry in Bible Atlas, so it cannot be linked.
In 6:47-49 the disciples' boat is out "in the middle of the sea" and Jesus walks on it; this is the Sea of Galilee, between Bethsaida and Gennesaret. Bible Atlas does not link it here.

Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but "the far side of the Jordan" in 10:1 is the land east of the river facing Judea, on the way to Jericho, so no dot is drawn.

"Caesar" in 12:14-17 is the emperor reigning at the time, Tiberius (AD 14-37), whose head and name were on the denarius; Bible Atlas's own entry for Tiberius names these verses but does not link them.

Some later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "spoken of by Daniel the prophet" in 13:14; the oldest manuscripts and this text do not name Daniel. The phrase "abomination of desolation" does come from Daniel 9:27, 11:31 and 12:11, as the chapter's notes explain.
In 14:67 the slave girl calls Jesus "that Nazarene", the man from Nazareth; Bible Atlas links Nazareth for the same word in 10:47 and 16:6 but not here.
Bible Atlas's "Place" entry is a duplicate of Golgotha, "Skull Place" (15:22), which is already linked.
